newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine exporters said sold 2.5-3.0 mln T wheat.
newsitem.headline: Argentine exporters said sold 2.5-3.0 mln T wheat.

text.p: Argentine exporters have sold between 2.5 million and 3.0 million tonnes of 1996/97 wheat, with the biggest sales going to traditional market Brazil, an export market analyst said Wednesday.

The analyst, who did not want to be identified, said that Brazilian and Paraguayan buyers had ordered 800,000 tonnes of wheat between them. Peru and Bolivia have ordered a total 180,000 tonnes and Cuba 100,000 tonnes, he said.
Buyers in Venezuela, Chile, the Dominican Republic and Colombia have each signed up for 50,000 tonnes.

The analyst said Indonesia had bought 300,000 tonnes so far this season and Malaysia 150,000 tonnes. Egypt has 200,000 tonnes, Turkey 100,000 tonnes, Tunisia 100,000 tonnes, and Iran between 100,000 tonnes and 200,000 tonnes.
Kenya has 50,000 tonnes, and other buyers in East Africa, including the Sudan, have bought 200,000 tonnes. South Africa has ordered 50,000 tonnes.
Traders Wednesday also said that Algeria had bought from 25,000 tonnes to 50,000 tonnes for December delivery.
But the analyst warned the Algerian purchase may well turn out to be an optional origin contract with French wheat.

Argentina is expected to harvest a bumper wheat crop, with most traders expecting 14 million tonnes or more. This would mean exports would double from last season to eight million or nine million tonnes.
